---
title: "1. Linear Stability"
sidebar: usage
jupyter: python3
---

The simplest dynamical system illustrating stability:

$$
\dot x = a\,x
$$

For $a > 0$ the origin is unstable (exponential growth). For $a < 0$ it is
linearly stable (exponential decay). At $a = 0$ the system loses hyperbolicity.

We define the system inline as a TVBO `Dynamics` and integrate it via the
class's own [`.plot()`](../Visualization.qmd) method:

```{python}
from tvbo import Dynamics
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

LIN_YAML = """
name: LinearScalar
description: |
  Scalar linear ODE $\\dot x = a x$. Stability of the origin is governed by
  the sign of $a$.
parameters:
  a:
    name: a
    value: 1.0
state_variables:
  x:
    name: x
    domain: { lo: -5.0, hi: 5.0 }
    equation:
      lhs: Derivative(x, t)
      rhs: a*x
    initial_value: 1.0
"""

dyn_unstable = Dynamics.from_string(LIN_YAML)
dyn_unstable.parameters['a'].value = 1.0

dyn_stable = Dynamics.from_string(LIN_YAML)
dyn_stable.parameters['a'].value = -1.0
```

## Reproducing `ExpExample0Red.png`

Both trajectories start at $x_0 = 1$ and are integrated for $4$ time units.

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4))
dyn_unstable.plot("x", duration=4, dt=1e-3, ax=ax)
dyn_stable.plot("x", duration=4, dt=1e-3, ax=ax)
ax.set_xlabel("Time $t$"); ax.set_ylabel("$x(t)$")
ax.set_ylim(-0.2, 4)
ax.lines[0].set_label("$a=1$")
ax.lines[1].set_label("$a=-1$")
ax.legend(handlelength=1)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Reproducing `ExpExamplePert.png`

Same system, but starting from a tiny perturbation $\delta = 10^{-6}$ applied
at $t = 1$:

```{python}
import numpy as np

tv = np.linspace(0, 4, 1000)
n4 = tv.size // 4
delta = 1e-6
x_pos = np.zeros_like(tv); x_pos[n4:] = delta * np.exp(tv[n4:] - tv[n4])
x_neg = np.zeros_like(tv); x_neg[n4:] = delta * np.exp(-(tv[n4:] - tv[n4]))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4))
ax.axhline(0, color="#c9211e", linestyle="--")
ax.plot(tv, x_pos, color="C0", lw=2, label="$a=1$")
ax.plot(tv, x_neg, color="C1", lw=2, label="$a=-1$")
ax.set_xlabel("Time $t$"); ax.set_ylabel("$x(t)$")
ax.set_ylim(-0.2 * 1e-5 / 4, 1e-5)
ax.legend(handlelength=1)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The qualitative behaviour is identical to the un-perturbed case: the only
information that survives a small perturbation of an unstable trajectory is
the sign of $a$. This motivates the local-flow / linearisation viewpoint
explored in the next section.
